newsitem.title: USA: China may have bought 50,000 T U.S. soymeal-trade.
newsitem.headline: China may have bought 50,000 T U.S. soymeal-trade.

text.p: Indications are that China bought at least 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal overnight for October shipment, U.S. exporters said.
One exporter said China bought 44 percent protein meal. Another exporter was unable to confirm the quantity but said China did buy soymeal.
"For the nearbys, the Chinese have been buying U.S. meal. This has been in the market for a few days," he said. "I do not know how much."
Rumors in the U.S. soybean market at mid-week had China seeking 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal.
"I think I have heard most of those rumors for the past couple of days," a third U.S. exporter said.
He said he would not be surprised if China bought 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes U.S. soymeal. "I think probably something is going on, but I just cannot confirm it," he said.
He said he anticipated strong Chinese interest for U.S. soymeal during 1996/97.

"We are still trying to zero in on the figures, but China is expected to buy somewhere around one million tonnes (optional origin soymeal) for the year with maybe 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes from the U.S," the exporter said.
China has not purchased U.S. soybeans so far this season, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. In 1995/96, U.S. soybean shipments to China were 422,800 tonnes.

Traders throughout the Far East have told Reuters they expect China to import between one million and 1.2 million tonnes of soybean meal in 1996. They said 600,000 tonnes should have arrived at Chinese ports by mid-September.
Asian traders are anticipating a soymeal price war once Chinese buyers return from their National Day holiday.

Soymeal futures on the Chicago Board of Trade dropped in the front months on Friday in line with lower CBOT soybeans and harvest pressure in the U.S. Midwest. At 1051 CDT, October soymeal was off $2.30 to ask at $245.40 a ton.

"This could be a big soybean harvest weekend," a U.S. trader said. But he noted that recent soybean and product sales of probably optional origin to the Chinese may have been done a while ago and traders were just now reporting them.
"Right now, we are quoting U.S. soybeans FOB, U.S. Gulf, for October/November shipment at $283.10 a tonne," the trader said.
